blocks.html: Thus he makes in his hearing an ample and true discourse (as has since appeared) of the country of the Basques, of the father, mother, brothers, sisters and other kinsfolk of Martin Guerre; of the year, month and day of his wedding; of his father-in-law and mother-in-law; of the persons who were there, and who negotiated the marriage; of the robes and garments with which each was then attired; of the priest who married them; of all the particular acts that took place there, both on the day of the wedding and before and after, even to setting down the persons who, about midnight of the wedding, went to visit him in his bed. Moreover, of his pretended child Sanxi Guerre, and of the day he was born; of the cause of his departure; of the persons he met on the way, and of the talk they had had together; of the places where he had stayed during his absence, both in Spain and in France; and of the persons whom he had approached in these two countries; and at each fact he particularly designates certain persons with whom inquiry can be made (as has since been done, and the whole verified), to render what he said still more persuasive and probable.
